content.title: About
content.content: Lemon juice 100 % is pure juice extracted from ripe lemons, pasteurized and packaged in glass or metal containers. It retains the characteristic tart flavor, aroma, and most of the vitamins, especially vitamin C.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lemons are among the oldest cultivated citrus fruits, with cultivation dating back over 2,500 years in Southeast Asia.
When pasteurized at low temperature and stored in dark bottles, the juice preserves almost all of its nutrients.
Lemon juice is widely used as a natural preservative in cooking because of its high acidity (pH ≈ 2.5).
In the United States, more than 30 % of all canned juices are lemon juice, often used in beverages and sauces.
Beyond culinary uses, lemon juice can help remove stains and odors around the house.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One cup (250 ml) of lemon juice provides over 150 % of the daily recommended vitamin C, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and citric acid act as antioxidants, helping neutralize free radicals and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity stimulates gastric juice production, improving food breakdown and nutrient absorption.

items.title: May reduce kidney stone risk
items.content: Citrate present in lemons can help prevent the formation of calcium oxalate stones.

items.title: Hydration and electrolytes
items.content: Lemon juice contains small amounts of potassium and magnesium, contributing to fluid‑electrolyte balance.

items.title: Acid reflux
items.content: People with gastro‑esophageal reflux disease (GERD) may experience worsened heartburn from highly acidic juice.

items.title: Tooth enamel erosion
items.content: Frequent consumption of undiluted lemon juice can erode dental enamel due to its acidity.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may develop allergic reactions to lemons, manifesting as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Acidity can affect the absorption of certain drugs, such as iron supplements.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lemon juice is used in drinks, marinades, sauces, baked goods, and desserts. It can be diluted in water, added to tea or cocktails, and used as a salad dressing. When drinking straight, it is advisable to dilute with water to lessen the acidity.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened containers in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if the color changes, an off‑odor develops, or mold appears.
